name: Mephibosheth
description: Jonathan's son living at the time of United Monarchy

points: Jonathan's son Mephibosheth was lame of his feet. When the tidings came of Saul and Jonathan out of Jezreel, he was five years old, and his nurse took him up and fled, and in her haste he fell and became lame.

Mephibosheth bowed himself and asked what David saw in such a dead dog as he was. David then called Ziba and gave unto his master's son all that pertained to Saul, and charged Ziba, his sons, and his servants to till the land and bring in the fruits, that Mephibosheth might have food, though he himself would eat at the king's table always.

Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants. This shows the level of riches Israel had as a nation: Saul's servant had servants of his own, that is how wealthy this man was, and all of them were set to till the land and take care of the house for Mephibosheth, all out of the respect David had for Jonathan.

note.label: 2 Samuel 9: David Shows Kindness for Jonathan's Sake

points: Mephibosheth had a young son named Micha, and all that dwelt in the house of Ziba were servants unto Mephibosheth, who dwelt in Jerusalem and did eat continually at the king's table, and was lame on both his feet.

note.label: 2 Samuel 9: David Shows Kindness for Jonathan's Sake

points: When David was past the top of the hill, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth met him with saddled asses, two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred bunches of raisins, a hundred summer fruits, and a bottle of wine. When David asked where his master's son was, Ziba said Mephibosheth abode in Jerusalem, saying the house of Israel would restore him the kingdom of his father. So David gave Ziba all that pertained to Mephibosheth.

Ziba came with gifts, and when David asked about Mephibosheth, Ziba claimed Mephibosheth thought the kingdom was about to be restored to him, which was not true. On that word David handed Ziba everything that belonged to Mephibosheth.

note.label: 2 Samuel 16: Ziba, Shimei's Cursing, and Absalom Defiles the Concubines

points: Mephibosheth the son of Saul came down to meet the king, having neither dressed his feet, trimmed his beard, nor washed his clothes from the day the king departed until he returned in peace, showing his mourning for David.

note.label: 2 Samuel 19: The King Returns to His House

points: David told him to speak no more of the matter and said that he and Ziba should divide the land. Mephibosheth answered that Ziba could take it all, for it was enough that his lord the king had come again in peace to his own house.

note.label: 2 Samuel 19: The King Returns to His House

points: The king spared Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, because of the Lord's oath that was between David and Jonathan. David did not go back on his oath; earlier he had promised Jonathan that his seed would always eat at David's table as long as there was family of the lineage of Jonathan.
